name: ADM1270ARQZ-R7
title: ADM1270: 4 V to 60 V input protection and hot swap controller for P-channel FETs
summary: The ADM1270 controls an external P-channel MOSFET in a 4 V to 60 V supply line to limit inrush and overcurrent, for modules plugged into live backplanes and for battery-powered gear. It senses current across a resistor, with a limit adjustable from 12.5 mV to 62.5 mV, folds the limit back as the output falls, and times how long the FET may stay in limit before latching off or retrying. It also drives a second P-channel FET as a low-drop reverse-polarity switch, and has UV, OV, enable, fault and power-good functions. Packages are a 16-lead QSOP and a 16-lead LFCSP of 3 mm × 3 mm; ADM1270ARQZ-R7 is the QSOP on a reel.

pins.name: VCAP
pins.function: Output of the internal 3.6 V regulator. Needs a capacitor of 1 µF or more for the part to hold its accuracy. Can serve as the top of a divider that sets the ISET voltage, or as a pull-up rail; keep its load at 100 µA or less to stay within its accuracy figures.

pins.name: ISET
pins.function: Sets the current-limit sense voltage. Tied straight to VCAP it selects the internal 2 V reference and the 50 mV default; a divider from VCAP or an outside reference sets any limit from 12.5 mV to 62.5 mV (VISET = 40 × VSENSE).

pins.name: UV
pins.function: Undervoltage comparator input, 1.0 V threshold. A divider from the supply brings the trip point onto this pin; below it the external FET is switched off.

pins.name: OV
pins.function: Overvoltage comparator input, 1.0 V threshold. A divider from the supply brings the trip point onto this pin; above it the external FET is switched off.

pins.name: ENABLE
pins.function: Logic enable. Must be high, along with valid UV and OV levels, before a power-up sequence starts; low keeps the controller off. No internal pull-up. Tied to FAULT it gives automatic retry.

pins.name: FAULT
pins.function: Fault flag, active low: goes low when the controller has shut the FET off after an overcurrent timeout. Wired to ENABLE, with a pull-up to VCAP, it makes the part retry by itself.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground.

pins.name: TIMER
pins.function: Capacitor CTIMER to ground sets how long the FET may sit in current limit. When the pin passes VTIMERH (2.0 V) the GATE is turned off.

pins.name: TIMER_OFF
pins.function: Capacitor CTIMER_OFF to ground sets the power-on delay before the first start and the off time after an overcurrent shutdown; the GATE stays off until this pin passes VTMROFFH (2.0 V).

pins.name: FB_PG
pins.function: Power-good comparator input, 1.0 V rising threshold with 30 mV hysteresis. A divider from the output voltage sets the level at which PWRGD is released.

pins.name: FLB
pins.function: Foldback input. A divider from the output lowers the current limit as the output falls, keeping the FET's dissipation inside its safe operating area. Clamped internally to 200 mV minimum so the limit never reaches zero.

pins.name: PWRGD
pins.function: Power-good output, open drain. Released high when FB_PG rises above 1 V; pulled low when FB_PG falls below 1 V less the hysteresis. Valid for VCC ≥ 1.7 V.

pins.name: GATE
pins.function: Drives the gate of the external P-channel pass FET. A pull-down current turns the FET on; the loop regulates this pin to hold the load current at the limit. Held off while the supply is below UVLO. Clamped to less than 14 V below VCC/SENSE+.

pins.name: SENSE−
pins.function: Low side of the current sense resistor; the same node feeds the pass FET. The sense voltage is VSENSE+ minus this pin. It also supplies part of the gate-drive bias.

pins.name: VCC/SENSE+
pins.function: Supply input, 4 V to 60 V, and the high side of the current sense resistor. Supplies most of the bias current. A UVLO circuit holds the part in reset and the GATE off at low supply. No supply sequencing needed.

pins.name: RPFG
pins.function: Gate drive for the external reverse-polarity P-channel FET, which replaces a series diode with a low-drop switch. Clamped to less than 14 V below VCC/SENSE+.

pins.name: EP
pins.function: Exposed pad on the underside of the LFCSP. Soldered to the board it carries heat away; it may be tied to ground.

pins.name: VCC/SENSE+
pins.function: Supply input, 4 V to 60 V, and the high side of the current sense resistor. Supplies most of the bias current. A UVLO circuit holds the part in reset and the GATE off at low supply. No supply sequencing needed.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A complete input protection stage between a supply VIN and a load. Q2, a P-channel FET driven from RPFG, sits first in the line as a low-drop reverse-polarity switch. RSENSE between VCC/SENSE+ and SENSE− measures load current, and the P-channel pass FET Q1, driven from GATE, limits it. R1, R2 and R3 form one string from the protected input to ground with UV and OV taps. R4 and R5 divide VCAP down to set the ISET voltage and so the current limit. R8, R7 and R9 form a string from VOUT to ground with the FLB tap above the FB_PG tap, giving foldback and the power-good level. CTIMER sets the time allowed in current limit and CTIMER_OFF the start-up delay and the off time after a fault. ENABLE, FAULT and PWRGD leave the circuit as control and status lines.
notes: Q2 has its drain on VIN and its source on the protected rail; Q1 has its source on SENSE− and its drain on VOUT.

circuits.title: Fixed 50 mV current sense limit
circuits.description: ISET tied directly to VCAP selects the internal 2 V reference, which gives a 50 mV current-sense limit across RSENSE. C1 bypasses VCAP to ground. The supply, 4 V to 60 V, enters at VCC/SENSE+; Q1 passes current from SENSE− to the output under control of GATE. FLB is left unconnected in this configuration.

circuits.title: Adjustable 12.5 mV to 62.5 mV current sense limit
circuits.description: A divider R1 over R2 from VCAP to ground sets the ISET voltage, and the current-sense limit follows as VISET / 40, anywhere from 12.5 mV to 62.5 mV. C1 bypasses VCAP. The power path is the same as in the fixed-limit case: RSENSE from the 4 V to 60 V supply to SENSE−, then the pass FET Q1 driven from GATE. FLB is left unconnected.

circuits.title: Undervoltage and overvoltage supply monitoring
circuits.description: One three-resistor string, R1, R2 and R3, runs from the 4 V to 60 V supply to ground. The R1-R2 junction feeds UV and the R2-R3 junction feeds OV, each compared against 1 V inside the part; the FET Q1 is turned off when the supply leaves the window. RSENSE and Q1 form the usual current-limited power path.

circuits.title: UV pin used as an enable
circuits.description: The UV divider R1 over R2 stays in place, and a system controller's open-drain enable line pulls the UV node low through D1. When the controller's transistor Q1 turns on, D1 conducts and UV drops below its 1 V threshold, turning the hot swap off; when Q1 is off, the controller's own pull-up R3 cannot raise UV because D1 blocks it, so the divider alone sets the threshold. D1 is chosen so that its forward drop plus the enable line's low level stay well under 1.0 V at IF = VIN/R1. With no pull-up on the open-drain line the diode is not needed.

parts.note: open-drain driver inside the system controller

circuits.title: Generation of the PWRGD signal
circuits.description: A divider RPG1 over RPG2 from the output to ground feeds FB_PG; PWRGD is released once the output is above 1 V × (1 + RPG1/RPG2). The supply side carries the R1, R2, R3 string for the UV and OV windows, RSENSE in the supply line and the pass FET Q1 driven from GATE.

operation.text: Plugging a board into a powered backplane lets empty bypass capacitors draw a surge that can burn connector contacts and pull the shared supply down far enough to reset neighbouring boards. The ADM1270 controls this surge with an external P-channel FET, limits steady overcurrent, and with a second P-channel FET blocks a reversed input.
VCC/SENSE+ takes 4 V to 60 V and supplies most of the bias. The rest, used for the gate drive and for regulating VGS closely, comes through SENSE−.
The drop across RSENSE, between VCC/SENSE+ and SENSE−, is amplified 40 times and compared with the current-limit reference. The GATE loop then holds the load current at the limit.
A selector watches ISET and FLB all the time and uses whichever is lower as the reference. In normal running ISET sets the limit; during start-up or a fault, a falling FLB takes over and lowers it.

The sense voltage limit can be set from 12.5 mV to 62.5 mV, which helps when very small sense resistor values are hard to obtain. ISET tied to VCAP selects the internal 2 V reference and a 50 mV limit. For any other value, a divider from the 3.6 V VCAP rail sets VISET = 40 × VSENSE. ISET above VISETRSTH (2.6 V typ) switches to the internal reference. VCAP may also pull up other pins, but loading it beyond 100 µA spoils its accuracy.

With the supply steady, the output voltage tells how much voltage the FET is dropping. A divider from the output to FLB, sized to give VISET/2 at the output level below which the limit should start to fall, makes the current limit shrink as the output falls, keeping FET dissipation down at start-up, in overload and in a short, so a smaller FET can be used. The trip level should sit well below the rail's normal tolerance. FLB is clamped at 200 mV, which is 10 mV across the sense resistor, so the current never folds back to zero; raising or lowering VISET moves that floor as a fraction of full current, for example VISET = 1.6 V puts it at 25 %.

CTIMER is charged by 20 µA and discharged by 1 µA, between thresholds of 0.1 V (VTIMERL) and 2.0 V (VTIMERH). When the sense voltage reaches the circuit-breaker level VCB, slightly below the regulation limit by VCBOS, the 20 µA source starts and the part regulates current. If the overload clears before 2.0 V, the 1 µA sink takes over, and below VTIMERL a strong pull-down empties the pin. If it lasts until 2.0 V, the GATE is switched off and FAULT is pulled low at once. The FET is chosen so that its safe operating area covers this time at the limit current; foldback eases that choice.

Without automatic retry, TIMER is discharged as it reaches VTIMERH and TIMER_OFF starts to charge. Until TIMER_OFF passes VTMROFFH the controller stays off and FAULT stays low; after that, taking ENABLE low and then high again restarts it.

When VCC appears, VCAP comes up quickly; once it passes UVLO the part leaves reset, with GATE and TIMER held low during that short period. An initial timing cycle follows: TIMER_OFF charges at 20 µA to 2.0 V. If UV and OV show VCC in range at the end, the hot swap begins. From then on TIMER_OFF times the off period after a fault, charging at 1 µA from the moment TIMER passes 2.0 V until it reaches VTMROFFH.

Connecting FAULT to ENABLE, with a pull-up from FAULT to VCAP, makes the part restart on its own. After a timeout turns the FET off, TIMER_OFF charges at 1 µA and the hot swap starts again when it reaches 2.0 V. The ratio of the two currents and of the two capacitors sets the duty cycle: 100 nF on each gives 10 ms on and 200 ms off. Retry repeats indefinitely; holding ENABLE low or breaking the FAULT link stops it. A larger CTIMER_OFF lengthens the off time to limit FET heating.
Both gate drivers are clamped to less than 14 V below VCC/SENSE+, which keeps both FETs inside their gate-source voltage limit.

Q2, driven from RPFG, guards both the ADM1270 and the load. With the supply reversed, so that VCC sits below system ground, the gate of Q2 is at GND and Q2 stays off; no reverse current flows and VOUT cannot go below ground. With normal polarity the gate is pulled down and Q2 conducts forward with low on-resistance, dropping less than a diode would and leaving more headroom and efficiency.
A second, fast current-sense amplifier catches short circuits: at roughly twice the normal limit the current is brought under control in about 2 µs.
UV and OV are compared with an internal 1 V reference, each fed from a resistor divider on the supply. UV below 1 V, or OV above 1 V, turns the FET off with the 10 mA gate pull-up.

ENABLE is a separate logic input that can hold the part off even when UV is above 1.0 V and OV below 1.0 V, so UV stays free for undervoltage monitoring. All three conditions must be met before power-up starts. UV can be used as an enable instead; to keep the UV divider as well, a diode from UV to the open-drain enable line isolates the line's pull-up from the divider.
PWRGD is open drain. It is released once FB_PG rises above 1 V and pulls low when FB_PG drops below 1 V minus a fixed 30 mV hysteresis. Its state is valid down to VCC = 1.7 V.
The LFCSP pad underneath should be soldered to the board for heat removal; it may be connected to ground.
